title: Magnons and excitons from Bethe-Salpeter equation and its application to graphene-based magnets
authors: Simran Chourasia, Maurício F. C. Martins Quintela, J. J. Palacios
abstract: With the recent isolation of two-dimensional semiconducting magnetic materials, the theoretical study of spin-flip collective excitations (magnons) along with spin-conserving electron-hole bound pairs (excitons) has become particularly relevant. Describing both types of quasiparticles within the same theoretical framework is possible, in principle, but the well-established many-body formalism for the calculation of excitons, based on the intertwined Bethe-Salpeter and Hedin's equations, is not satisfactory for magnons, since the usual approximations produce a spurious gapped Goldstone mode. Here, we show that excitons and magnons can be computed on the same footing under the same Bethe-Salpeter formalism, while respecting the gapless Goldstone mode for magnons. We demonstrate how this can be achieved through the evaluation of the full Bethe-Salpeter equation, beyond the Tamm-Dancoff approximation in model Hamiltonians. As an example, we apply it to ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic graphene, faithfully represented by the extended Hubbard model. Our results clarify the roles of on-site and non-local interactions in exciton and magnon appearance and identify consistency requirements relevant to extending the approach to first-principles calculations.
summary: This paper develops a unified theoretical approach using the full Bethe-Salpeter Equation to calculate both excitons and magnons in 2D magnetic materials. By going beyond standard approximations, the authors resolve the theoretical inconsistency that previously caused the magnon's Goldstone mode to appear gapped. This provides a robust tool for understanding coupled spin-charge physics in systems like graphene magnets.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a unified theoretical framework to describe both spin-flip collective excitations (magnons) and spin-conserving electron-hole bound pairs (excitons) in magnetic materials.
main_result: The authors successfully show that excitons and magnons can be calculated using the same full Bethe-Salpeter formalism, crucially correcting the standard approximation that incorrectly gaps the magnon's Goldstone mode.
method: The methodology involves extending the Bethe-Salpeter Equation (BSE) beyond the Tamm-Dancoff approximation, utilizing the full many-body formalism to treat both types of excitations consistently.
model_or_system: The study applies this formalism to model Hamiltonians, specifically using the extended Hubbard model to represent ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic graphene, which are prototypical 2D semiconducting magnetic materials.
key_observables: Exciton energy (bound pairs), magnon dispersion (spin-flip excitations), and the zero-energy Goldstone mode.
important_parameters: On-site and non-local interaction strengths ($U$, $J$), and the magnetic ordering (ferromagnetic vs. antiferromagnetic).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the full BSE formalism, when correctly implemented, can treat the gapless nature of the magnon mode while simultaneously capturing the physics of excitons.
figures_summary: Figure 9 is noted to show the wave functions of the Goldstone magnon and the lowest bright exciton for ferromagnetic graphene at various high-symmetry points ($\Gamma, M, K/K'$), comparing results from BSE/TDA and BSE/RPA.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the BSE forms, focuses on applying the methodology to model Hamiltonians, and concludes with an application to magnetic graphene.
why_interesting: The ability to treat spin dynamics (magnons) and charge excitations (excitons) within one consistent, gap-correcting framework is vital for understanding coupled spin-charge dynamics in 2D spintronic materials.

The dashed circle around the leftmost atomic site indicates the position of the added Hydrogen atom. Lattice vectors a1/2 correspond to doubling the lattice vectors of the standard graphene lattice.

FIG. 2. Single-particle non-interacting (left panel) and unrestricted Hartree-Fock quasi-particle (right panel) band structure for ferromagnetic hydrogenated graphene system with 8 Carbon atoms per unit cell. In the right hand side plot, solid lines correspond to an UHF calculation with U = 4 eV and J = 1.25 eV, while dashed lines have J = 0 eV. Quasi-particle gaps between the three distinct band pairings relevant are highlighted by the transitions in question.

FIG. 3. Effects of including only on-site versus off-site on the excitation energies in the BSE/TDA formalism. First six eigenvalues included in each spin sector, separated by the vertical dashed lines as ↑↓, ↓↓, and ↑↑. Horizontal dashed lines correspond to the bandgap for each of these sectors.
FIG. 5. Magnon dispersion from UHF computed via BSE/TDA (black lines) or BSE/RPA (red dashed lines) for COM momentum Q along the K-Γ-M-K′-Γ-K path in the first Brillouin zone.

FIG. 4. Magnon (black lines) and exciton (blue and red lines) dispersion for COM momentum Q along the K-Γ-M- K′-Γ-K path in the first Brillouin zone with BSE/TDA. Black lines highlight the magnon Goldstone mode and the optical magnons, grey lines are the Stoner continuum. Solid dots at Γ in the exciton lines denotes an optically bright state. Excitons depicted in blue/red correspond to transitions associated with the band pairings denoted as E↓↓/E↑↑in Fig. (2), respectively.
